blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.text: Abstract

blocks.en: Through a map and sound physicalization, we invite the public to see, feel, and interact with patterns of environmental stress in Taiwan rather than reading data tables.
blocks.text: Through a map and sound physicalization, we invite the public to see, feel, and interact with patterns of environmental stress in Taiwan rather than reading data tables.
blocks.zh: 我們以一張地圖與一組聲音實體化，邀請大眾去看見、感受並親手互動臺灣各地的環境逆境樣貌，而不是讀資料表。

blocks.en: Climate data can be difficult to understand through numbers alone. To make the effects of climate change on agriculture more tangible, we developed a Data Physicalization Map using styrofoam, colored paper, and LED lights to visualize crop yields and stress levels across Taiwan. We also created a Sound Physicalization website that allows visitors to hear representations of plant stress. Through our exhibition, we reached 116 visitors and collected 62 survey responses, with 95.2% (59 of 62) agreeing that these tools helped them better understand the relationship between climate change and crop yield. By turning scientific data into experiences people can see and hear, we hope to make agricultural challenges more accessible and meaningful to the public.

blocks.zh: 光看數字，氣候資料並不容易理解。為了讓氣候變遷對農業的影響更具體，我們以保麗龍、色紙與 LED 燈做出一張數據實體化地圖，把全臺的作物產量與逆境程度視覺化。我們也做了一個聲音實體化網站，讓參觀者聽見植物逆境的呈現。透過這場展示，我們接觸到 116 位參觀者、收回 62 份問卷，其中 95.2%（62 人中的 59 人）同意這些工具幫助他們更理解氣候變遷與作物產量之間的關係。把科學數據變成看得見、聽得到的體驗，我們希望讓農業面臨的難題對大眾更可親、也更有意義。

blocks.en: Overview

blocks.en: Data Physicalization
blocks.text: Data Physicalization
blocks.zh: 數據實體化

blocks.en: Data physicalization is the practice of transforming abstract datasets into tangible physical artifacts, such as models, sculptures, or interactive maps. Instead of viewing numbers on a 2D screen or standard graph, people can interact with data through their senses. By using physical elements like colors, lights, and sound to represent real-world variables, data physicalization bridges the gap between complex information and human intuition, making critical insights much more accessible, memorable, and impactful.
blocks.text: Data physicalization is the practice of transforming abstract datasets into tangible physical artifacts, such as models, sculptures, or interactive maps. Instead of viewing numbers on a 2D screen or standard graph, people can interact with data through their senses. By using physical elements like colors, lights, and sound to represent real-world variables, data physicalization bridges the gap between complex information and human intuition, making critical insights much more accessible, memorable, and impactful.
blocks.zh: 數據實體化是把抽象的資料集轉成可觸摸的實體物件，例如模型、雕塑或互動地圖。人們不必在 2D 螢幕或標準圖表上看數字，而能用自己的感官與資料互動。藉由顏色、燈光與聲音這類實體元素來代表真實世界的變數，數據實體化在複雜資訊與人的直覺之間搭起橋梁，讓關鍵的洞見更容易取得、更容易記住，也更有力量。

blocks.en: Goals
blocks.text: Goals
blocks.zh: 目標

blocks.en: Climate change is putting more heat and drought stress on Taiwan’s crops, but people often do not notice it until prices of certain food crops start to rise in the market. To really feel the gravity of climate warnings and make their effects on plants more tangible, we developed a data physicalization map and a website where the public can hear the sound plants make when facing stress. Through the creation of a map and sound physicalization, we invite the public to see, feel, and interact with patterns of environmental stress throughout Taiwan rather than reading data tables and graphs. With data physicalization, we aim to make the interaction between agriculture, climate, and plant stress more accessible and easy to understand.
blocks.text: Climate change is putting more heat and drought stress on Taiwan’s crops, but people often do not notice it until prices of certain food crops start to rise in the market. To really feel the gravity of climate warnings and make their effects on plants more tangible, we developed a data physicalization map and a website where the public can hear the sound plants make when facing stress. Through the creation of a map and sound physicalization, we invite the public to see, feel, and interact with patterns of environmental stress throughout Taiwan rather than reading data tables and graphs. With data physicalization, we aim to make the interaction between agriculture, climate, and plant stress more accessible and easy to understand.
blocks.zh: 氣候變遷讓臺灣的作物承受更多熱逆境與乾旱逆境，但人們往往要等到某些食用作物在市場上漲價，才會注意到。為了讓氣候警訊的分量被真正感受到、讓它對植物的影響更具體，我們做了一張數據實體化地圖，以及一個能讓大眾聽見植物面臨逆境時所發出聲音的網站。透過地圖與聲音的實體化，我們邀請大眾去看見、感受並互動臺灣各地的環境逆境樣貌，而不是讀資料表與圖。藉由數據實體化，我們希望讓農業、氣候與植物逆境之間的關係更容易接近、也更容易理解。

blocks.en: Why physicalize?
blocks.text: Why physicalize?
blocks.zh: 為什麼要實體化？

blocks.en: “A data physicalization (or simply physicalization) is a physical artifact whose geometry or material properties encode data” (Jansen). Data physicalization helps people communicate and understand data through physical representations. These visualizations help convey the data in a more accessible way (Jansen). Our data map physicalization is a type of physical visualization where map data are converted to a physical form.
blocks.text: “A data physicalization (or simply physicalization) is a physical artifact whose geometry or material properties encode data” (Jansen). Data physicalization helps people communicate and understand data through physical representations. These visualizations help convey the data in a more accessible way (Jansen). Our data map physicalization is a type of physical visualization where map data are converted to a physical form.
blocks.zh: 「數據實體化（或簡稱實體化）是一件實體物件，它的幾何或材料性質把資料編碼在其中」（Jansen）。數據實體化幫助人們透過實體的呈現來溝通與理解資料，這類視覺化讓資料以更易於接近的方式被傳達（Jansen）。我們的數據地圖實體化屬於實體視覺化的一種：把地圖資料轉換成實體形式。

blocks.en: The data
blocks.text: The data
blocks.zh: 資料

blocks.en: Rather than selecting data solely because it was readily available, we considered which variables could best communicate the environmental stresses relevant to our project and our target agricultural communities. The board uses two county-level datasets: rice yield and heat stress. We chose heat because it is one of the stresses ReLEAF protects against, and yield because it shows what that stress costs farmers. We first found the patterns in the data that matter most for plant stress, then chose a physical feature of the map to show each one. This allowed every component of our map to remain connected to the dataset, making the information easier to understand through physical interaction.
blocks.text: Rather than selecting data solely because it was readily available, we considered which variables could best communicate the environmental stresses relevant to our project and our target agricultural communities. The board uses two county-level datasets: rice yield and heat stress. We chose heat because it is one of the stresses ReLEAF protects against, and yield because it shows what that stress costs farmers. We first found the patterns in the data that matter most for plant stress, then chose a physical feature of the map to show each one. This allowed every component of our map to remain connected to the dataset, making the information easier to understand through physical interaction.
blocks.zh: 我們並不是因為某份資料容易取得就選它，而是考慮哪些變數最能傳達與我們的專題、以及目標農業社群相關的環境逆境。這塊板子使用兩組縣市層級的資料：稻作產量與熱逆境。選熱逆境，是因為它正是 ReLEAF 所保護的逆境之一；選產量，是因為它顯示這份逆境讓農友付出了什麼代價。我們先在資料中找出對植物逆境最重要的樣態，再為每一個樣態選一項地圖上的實體特徵來表現它。如此一來，地圖的每個元件都與資料集保持連結，也讓資訊透過實體互動更容易被理解。

blocks.en: From data to map
blocks.text: From data to map
blocks.zh: 從資料到地圖

blocks.en: Paper color shows crop yield and flashing LEDs represent plant stress severity. Through this combination, viewers can visually compare areas with different agricultural conditions. Many visitors expected Taipei to show the most stress, and asked why Yilan and Nantou did. Nantou sits against the steep central mountains, where erratic rainfall and typhoons cost crops through landslides, and Yilan sits on the coast, where salinity is higher.
blocks.text: Paper color shows crop yield and flashing LEDs represent plant stress severity. Through this combination, viewers can visually compare areas with different agricultural conditions. Many visitors expected Taipei to show the most stress, and asked why Yilan and Nantou did. Nantou sits against the steep central mountains, where erratic rainfall and typhoons cost crops through landslides, and Yilan sits on the coast, where salinity is higher.
blocks.zh: 紙的顏色顯示作物產量，閃爍的 LED 代表植物逆境的嚴重程度。透過這個組合，觀看者可以直接比較不同農業條件的地區。許多參觀者以為臺北的逆境會最嚴重，於是問我們為什麼是宜蘭與南投。南投緊靠著陡峭的中央山脈，不穩定的降雨與颱風會以坍方的形式讓作物受損；宜蘭則臨海，鹽度較高。

blocks.en: For our sound component, instead of just showing data, we wanted participants to actually hear what sounds are made by plants under stress. Plants respond to stress in ways people cannot see, and few know that a plant under drought stress makes sounds. We therefore allowed participants to use headphones to listen to recordings of the sounds produced by tomato and tobacco plants experiencing drought stress. This gave participants an opportunity to understand plant stress through hearing rather than simply reading about it.
blocks.text: For our sound component, instead of just showing data, we wanted participants to actually hear what sounds are made by plants under stress. Plants respond to stress in ways people cannot see, and few know that a plant under drought stress makes sounds. We therefore allowed participants to use headphones to listen to recordings of the sounds produced by tomato and tobacco plants experiencing drought stress. This gave participants an opportunity to understand plant stress through hearing rather than simply reading about it.
blocks.zh: 至於聲音的部分，我們不只想把資料秀出來，而是希望參與者真的聽見植物在逆境下發出的聲音。植物以人看不見的方式回應逆境，而很少人知道，植物在乾旱逆境下會發出聲音。因此我們讓參與者戴上耳機，聆聽番茄與菸草在乾旱逆境下發出的聲音錄音。這讓參與者得以用聽的、而不只是讀的方式去理解植物逆境。

blocks.en: Concept and inspiration
blocks.text: Concept and inspiration
blocks.zh: 概念與靈感

blocks.en: Our data physicalization was inspired by the idea that scientific data should not only be seen, but also experienced. Plant stress is often difficult for people to understand because many of its effects occur at a microscopic or molecular level and cannot be directly observed. We wanted to transform these invisible changes into interactive experiences that could make plant stress more tangible and accessible to the public.
blocks.text: Our data physicalization was inspired by the idea that scientific data should not only be seen, but also experienced. Plant stress is often difficult for people to understand because many of its effects occur at a microscopic or molecular level and cannot be directly observed. We wanted to transform these invisible changes into interactive experiences that could make plant stress more tangible and accessible to the public.
blocks.zh: 我們的數據實體化來自一個想法：科學資料不該只是被看見，也該被經驗。植物逆境常讓人難以理解，因為它的許多效應發生在顯微或分子層次，無法直接觀察。我們想把這些看不見的變化轉成互動的體驗，讓植物逆境對大眾更具體、也更容易接近。

blocks.en: Our physicalizations were designed around different ways of experiencing data, including visual representations and hands-on interaction. By translating scientific information into sensory experiences, participants could explore how plants respond to environmental stress rather than simply reading about it on a poster. This approach also reflects the core idea of our ReLEAF project: connecting complex biological signals with information that people can easily understand and respond to.
blocks.text: Our physicalizations were designed around different ways of experiencing data, including visual representations and hands-on interaction. By translating scientific information into sensory experiences, participants could explore how plants respond to environmental stress rather than simply reading about it on a poster. This approach also reflects the core idea of our ReLEAF project: connecting complex biological signals with information that people can easily understand and respond to.
blocks.zh: 我們的實體化作品是圍繞著不同的資料經驗方式設計的，包括視覺呈現與動手互動。把科學資訊轉譯成感官體驗，參與者就能去探索植物如何回應環境逆境，而不只是在海報上讀到它。這個做法也呼應 ReLEAF 專題的核心想法：把複雜的生物訊號，連到人們容易理解並做出回應的資訊。

blocks.en: We created the physical map using styrofoam as the base material, with different colored papers placed on top to represent variations in crop yield. LED lights were incorporated into the map to visualize plant stress levels. The map shows the different regions and turns the data into something tangible.
blocks.text: We created the physical map using styrofoam as the base material, with different colored papers placed on top to represent variations in crop yield. LED lights were incorporated into the map to visualize plant stress levels. The map shows the different regions and turns the data into something tangible.

blocks.en: For the sound physicalization, participants were provided with headphones and invited to listen to recordings of drought-stressed tomato and tobacco plants. Instead of visually representing the data, this activity allowed participants to hear signals associated with plant responses to drought stress.
blocks.text: For the sound physicalization, participants were provided with headphones and invited to listen to recordings of drought-stressed tomato and tobacco plants. blocks.zh: 在聲音實體化的部分，我們提供耳機，邀請參與者聆聽番茄與菸草在乾旱逆境下的錄音。這項活動不以視覺呈現資料，而是讓參與者聽見與植物乾旱逆境反應有關的訊號。

blocks.en: By combining a physical map with an auditory experience, we created two different ways for participants to interact with otherwise invisible plant-stress information.
blocks.text: By combining a physical map with an auditory experience, we created two different ways for participants to interact with otherwise invisible plant-stress information.

blocks.zh: 與大眾的互動

blocks.en: Throughout the booth, visitors were curious about why Yilan and Nantou had the highest stress. Many believed that regions such as Taipei would have the most stress instead. We explained that tourism in Nantou and Yilan was affecting their stress levels, along with their geography, with Nantou being located near the steep mountainous range where crops are prone to loss through landslides caused by erratic rainfall as well as typhoons and Yilan being located right by the coast where salinity levels are higher. Visitors vocalized their curiosity when they noticed our poster since the data may not align with what they had thought the most affected regions were.

We explained that tourism in Nantou and Yilan was affecting their stress levels, along with their geography, with Nantou being located near the steep mountainous range where crops are prone to loss through landslides caused by erratic rainfall as well as typhoons and Yilan being located right by the coast where salinity levels are higher. blocks.zh: 整個攤位期間，參觀者都很好奇為什麼宜蘭與南投的逆境最高。許多人以為臺北之類的地區逆境才最嚴重。我們解釋，南投與宜蘭的觀光，加上它們的地理條件，都影響了逆境程度：南投靠近陡峭的山脈，作物容易因不穩定降雨與颱風引發的坍方而損失；宜蘭則緊鄰海岸，鹽度較高。參觀者看到我們的海報時紛紛說出自己的疑惑，因為資料與他們原本以為受影響最嚴重的地區並不一致。

blocks.en: Feedback
blocks.text: Feedback
blocks.zh: 回饋

blocks.en: Visitors told us the flashing lights made high-stress areas easy to spot. Through this, we were able to teach the Taiwanese public more about their own country and inform them about the effects climate change has on our local agriculture.
blocks.text: Visitors told us the flashing lights made high-stress areas easy to spot. Through this, we were able to teach the Taiwanese public more about their own country and inform them about the effects climate change has on our local agriculture.
blocks.zh: 參觀者告訴我們，閃爍的燈讓高逆境地區很容易一眼認出。藉此，我們也讓臺灣民眾更認識自己的土地，並了解氣候變遷對在地農業造成的影響。

blocks.en: Translation

blocks.en: I learned that Yilan County has the highest plant stress
blocks.text: I learned that Yilan County has the highest plant stress
blocks.zh: 我學到宜蘭縣的植物逆境最高

blocks.en: Sound of plants
blocks.text: Sound of plants
blocks.zh: 植物的聲音

blocks.en: Concept and inspiration
blocks.text: Concept and inspiration
blocks.zh: 概念與靈感

blocks.en: Plants respond to stress in ways that are often invisible to the human eye until visible damage has already occurred, but recent research has shown that some of these responses aren't entirely silent. Under drought stress, plants can produce ultrasonic clicking sounds, signals that exist far outside the range of human hearing and go completely unnoticed in everyday life. We wanted to explore this hidden dimension of plant stress as a companion to our Data Physicalization Map: while the map translated environmental data into something visitors could see, we wanted to give people a way to actually hear plant stress for themselves. By making these normally imperceptible signals audible, we hoped to make the experience of plant stress feel immediate and real, rather than abstract, and to reinforce ReLEAF's core idea that stress can be detected and responded to before it becomes visible, irreversible damage.
blocks.text: Plants respond to stress in ways that are often invisible to the human eye until visible damage has already occurred, but recent research has shown that some of these responses aren't entirely silent. Under drought stress, plants can produce ultrasonic clicking sounds, signals that exist far outside the range of human hearing and go completely unnoticed in everyday life. We wanted to explore this hidden dimension of plant stress as a companion to our Data Physicalization Map: while the map translated environmental data into something visitors could see, we wanted to give people a way to actually hear plant stress for themselves. By making these normally imperceptible signals audible, we hoped to make the experience of plant stress feel immediate and real, rather than abstract, and to reinforce ReLEAF's core idea that stress can be detected and responded to before it becomes visible, irreversible damage.
blocks.zh: 植物回應逆境的方式，往往在出現肉眼可見的損傷之前都看不出來；但近期研究顯示，這些反應並不全然無聲。在乾旱逆境下，植物會發出超音波的喀嚓聲——這些訊號遠在人類聽覺範圍之外，日常生活中完全不會被注意到。我們想把植物逆境這個隱藏的面向，作為數據實體化地圖的搭檔加以探索：地圖把環境資料轉成參觀者看得見的東西，而我們想讓人們真的親耳聽見植物的逆境。把這些平常感知不到的訊號變成可聽見的，我們希望讓植物逆境的體驗變得直接而真實，而不是抽象的；也藉此強化 ReLEAF 的核心想法——逆境可以在變成看得見、不可逆的損傷之前就被偵測並回應。

blocks.en: The idea of letting visitors experience the sounds plants made under stress first started when we came across a scientific paper that focused on how plants make sounds that are not audible to humans under stress. After finding this paper, we realized how impactful it would be if the public realized how plants can also sense stress inflicted upon them. When facing drought stress, which is the stress that we presented during our public forum booth, plants experience a physical process called cavitation, where continuous water columns inside the plant snap and form air bubbles.
blocks.text: The idea of letting visitors experience the sounds plants made under stress first started when we came across a scientific paper that focused on how plants make sounds that are not audible to humans under stress. After finding this paper, we realized how impactful it would be if the public realized how plants can also sense stress inflicted upon them. When facing drought stress, which is the stress that we presented during our public forum booth, plants experience a physical process called cavitation, where continuous water columns inside the plant snap and form air bubbles.
blocks.zh: 讓參觀者體驗植物在逆境下發出的聲音，這個想法始於我們讀到一篇科學論文，講的是植物在逆境下會發出人類聽不見的聲音。讀完之後我們意識到，如果大眾能知道植物同樣感受得到加諸其上的逆境，那會是多麼有力的一件事。在乾旱逆境下——也就是我們在公開論壇攤位上呈現的那種逆境——植物體內會發生一種稱為空穴化（cavitation）的物理過程：植物體內連續的水柱斷裂，形成氣泡。

blocks.en: How researchers captured it:
blocks.text: How researchers captured it:
blocks.zh: 研究者如何捕捉到它：

blocks.en: Ultrasonic microphones.
blocks.text: Ultrasonic microphones.
blocks.zh: 超音波麥克風。

blocks.en: The pops sit far above human hearing, so Khait, Hadany et al. (Tel Aviv University) recorded across 20–250 kHz, about 10 cm from each plant.
blocks.text: The pops sit far above human hearing, so Khait, Hadany et al. (Tel Aviv University) recorded across 20–250 kHz, about 10 cm from each plant.
blocks.zh: 這些爆裂聲遠高於人類聽覺範圍，因此 Khait、Hadany 等人（特拉維夫大學）在距離每株植物約 10 cm 處，以 20–250 kHz 的範圍錄音。

blocks.en: A soundproofed chamber first.
blocks.text: A soundproofed chamber first.
blocks.zh: 先在隔音室裡。

blocks.en: Tomato and tobacco recorded three ways: untouched, five days without water, and freshly cut.
blocks.text: Tomato and tobacco recorded three ways: untouched, five days without water, and freshly cut.
blocks.zh: 番茄與菸草各以三種狀態錄音：未受擾動、五天未澆水，以及剛被切開。

blocks.en: Then a working greenhouse.
blocks.text: Then a working greenhouse.
blocks.zh: 接著在實際運作的溫室裡。

blocks.en: Repeated amid ordinary background noise to prove it wasn't a laboratory artifact.
blocks.text: Repeated amid ordinary background noise to prove it wasn't a laboratory artifact.
blocks.zh: 在一般背景噪音中重做一次，以證明這不是實驗室的人為產物。

blocks.en: Machine learning.
blocks.text: Machine learning.
blocks.zh: 機器學習。

blocks.en: A classifier trained on many acoustic features (not one number) separated stressed from healthy, drought from cutting, and tomato from tobacco.
blocks.text: A classifier trained on many acoustic features (not one number) separated stressed from healthy, drought from cutting, and tomato from tobacco.
blocks.zh: 以多項聲學特徵（而非單一數值）訓練的分類器，能分辨受逆境與健康、乾旱與切割，以及番茄與菸草。

blocks.en: Physicalization method
blocks.text: Physicalization method
blocks.zh: 實體化方法

blocks.en: To transform plant stress into an accessible sensory experience, we used the open recordings from Khait et al. (2023). The clicks are ultrasonic, so we shifted their pitch down into the range people can hear. We built a website to play them, and at the booth two headphones were connected to laptops hidden behind the poster. Participants could choose which plant they wanted to explore, either tobacco or tomato, and listen to their corresponding stress recordings through the headphones. By presenting plant stress through sound, we aimed to provide visitors with a more immersive way to understand that plants respond to environmental stress, even when these responses cannot be directly heard by humans.
blocks.text: To transform plant stress into an accessible sensory experience, we used the open recordings from Khait et al. (2023). The clicks are ultrasonic, so we shifted their pitch down into the range people can hear. We built a website to play them, and at the booth two headphones were connected to laptops hidden behind the poster. Participants could choose which plant they wanted to explore, either tobacco or tomato, and listen to their corresponding stress recordings through the headphones. By presenting plant stress through sound, we aimed to provide visitors with a more immersive way to understand that plants respond to environmental stress, even when these responses cannot be directly heard by humans.
blocks.zh: 為了把植物逆境變成可親的感官體驗，我們使用 Khait 等人（2023）公開的錄音。這些喀嚓聲屬於超音波，因此我們把音高往下移到人耳聽得見的範圍。我們做了一個網站來播放它們，並把兩副耳機接到藏在海報後方的筆電上。參與者可以選擇想探索的植物，番茄或菸草，透過耳機聆聽對應的逆境錄音。以聲音呈現植物逆境，我們希望讓參觀者以更沉浸的方式理解：即使人類無法直接聽見，植物確實會回應環境逆境。

blocks.en: Figure 3 Sound of plants played for the listener. Open the listening site to hear the tomato and tobacco recordings.
blocks.text: Figure 3 Sound of plants played for the listener. Open the listening site to hear the tomato and tobacco recordings.
blocks.zh: 圖 3 播給聆聽者的植物聲音。開啟聆聽網站即可聽見番茄與菸草的錄音。

blocks.en: Public interaction
blocks.text: Public interaction
blocks.zh: 與大眾的互動

blocks.en: When presenting our sound physicalization, many were fascinated with the fact that plants made noises when facing stress. We explained that a dry plant pulls hard on the water in its stem, and the water column can snap and form an air bubble. Each snap makes a pop, similar to the sound of bubble wrap. Overall, the public was intrigued with the demonstration and gave positive feedback.
blocks.text: When presenting our sound physicalization, many were fascinated with the fact that plants made noises when facing stress. We explained that a dry plant pulls hard on the water in its stem, and the water column can snap and form an air bubble. Each snap makes a pop, similar to the sound of bubble wrap. Overall, the public was intrigued with the demonstration and gave positive feedback.
blocks.zh: 在呈現聲音實體化時，許多人對「植物面臨逆境時會發出聲音」這件事深感著迷。我們解釋：缺水的植物會用力拉扯莖內的水，水柱可能因此斷裂、形成氣泡，每一次斷裂都發出一個爆裂聲，就像捏氣泡紙的聲音。整體而言，大眾對這項展示很感興趣，回饋也相當正面。

blocks.text: Figure 4 A young visitor listening to the sound of a drought-stressed plant.
blocks.zh: 圖 4 一位小小參觀者正在聆聽受乾旱逆境植物的聲音。

blocks.en: Feedback
blocks.text: Feedback
blocks.zh: 回饋

blocks.en: After they finished visiting our booth, visitors were asked to give feedback on the overall event. Most were fascinated or surprised by the fact that plants make clicking noises when they lack water, and some even mentioned how the sound physicalization was the most memorable part of the whole booth.
blocks.text: After they finished visiting our booth, visitors were asked to give feedback on the overall event. Most were fascinated or surprised by the fact that plants make clicking noises when they lack water, and some even mentioned how the sound physicalization was the most memorable part of the whole booth.
blocks.zh: 參觀完我們的攤位後，我們請參觀者對整場活動給予回饋。多數人對「植物缺水時會發出喀嚓聲」感到著迷或驚訝，有些人甚至提到，聲音實體化是整個攤位中最令人印象深刻的部分。

blocks.en: Impact
blocks.text: Impact
blocks.zh: 影響

blocks.en: At the end of the event, visitors who had been to all six booths filled in one survey. 62 of the 160 people who visited our booth answered it. The response rate reflects that many visitors attended as families with young children, so parents completed a single form on behalf of the entire group rather than having each individual submit one separately. Out of 160 total booth visitors, 62 completed the form.
blocks.text: At the end of the event, visitors who had been to all six booths filled in one survey. 62 of the 160 people who visited our booth answered it. The response rate reflects that many visitors attended as families with young children, so parents completed a single form on behalf of the entire group rather than having each individual submit one separately. Out of 160 total booth visitors, 62 completed the form.
blocks.zh: 活動結束時，走完全部六個攤位的參觀者填寫一份問卷。造訪我們攤位的 160 人中有 62 人填答。這個回收率反映出許多參觀者是帶著年幼孩子的家庭，父母會代表全家填一份，而不是每個人各填一份。在 160 位攤位參觀者中，共有 62 人完成問卷。

blocks.en: Connecting data to plant stress: knowledge
blocks.text: Connecting data to plant stress: knowledge
blocks.zh: 把資料連到植物逆境：知識

blocks.en: To test whether participants actually understood our physicalized data, we asked them to identify the region shown as experiencing the highest plant stress on our map. 32 of 62 respondents (51.6%) correctly identified Yilan County, the region we represented as highest-stress. The remaining responses were split across Kaohsiung (12, 19.4%), Taichung (11, 17.7%), and Tainan (7, 11.3%). Yilan’s high stress amount was showcased through its frequent flashing of LED lights.
blocks.text: To test whether participants actually understood our physicalized data, we asked them to identify the region shown as experiencing the highest plant stress on our map. 32 of 62 respondents (51.6%) correctly identified Yilan County, the region we represented as highest-stress. The remaining responses were split across Kaohsiung (12, 19.4%), Taichung (11, 17.7%), and Tainan (7, 11.3%). Yilan’s high stress amount was showcased through its frequent flashing of LED lights.
blocks.zh: 為了測試參與者是否真的理解我們實體化的資料，我們請他們指出地圖上顯示植物逆境最高的地區。62 位受訪者中有 32 位（51.6%）正確指出宜蘭縣，也就是我們呈現為逆境最高的地區。其餘答案分布在高雄（12 位，19.4%）、臺中（11 位，17.7%）與臺南（7 位，11.3%）。宜蘭的高逆境是透過 LED 燈頻繁閃爍來呈現的。

blocks.en: Just over half of visitors read the map correctly on a single, brief encounter: a reasonable result for a passive booth interaction, but it also points to a concrete design target. Next time, we will put a legend beside the board that shows three flash speeds and what each one means. We will then check whether more than 80% of visitors pick the right region, to showcase that our data physicalization actually conveyed information to the public.

blocks.en: Raising awareness: attitude
blocks.text: Raising awareness: attitude
blocks.zh: 提高意識：態度

blocks.en: Figure 6 Showcasing the percentage of participants that understood the impact of stress.
blocks.text: Figure 6 Showcasing the percentage of participants that understood the impact of stress.
blocks.zh: 圖 6 呈現理解逆境影響的參與者比例。

blocks.en: We then looked at whether the exhibit changed how participants understood the consequences of environmental stress for agriculture. 39 of 62 participants (62.9%) reported they now “very much understood” the impact of climate change on Taiwan's coffee and crop production, and another 21 (33.9%) said they understood it “partially.” Only 2 (3.2%) said they still didn't understand it well.
blocks.text: We then looked at whether the exhibit changed how participants understood the consequences of environmental stress for agriculture. 39 of 62 participants (62.9%) reported they now “very much understood” the impact of climate change on Taiwan's coffee and crop production, and another 21 (33.9%) said they understood it “partially.” Only 2 (3.2%) said they still didn't understand it well.
blocks.zh: 接著我們檢視這場展示是否改變了參與者對環境逆境後果的理解。62 位參與者中有 39 位（62.9%）表示自己現在「非常理解」氣候變遷對臺灣咖啡與作物生產的影響，另有 21 位（33.9%）表示「部分理解」。只有 2 位（3.2%）表示仍然不太理解。

blocks.en: 59 of 62 participants (95.2%) agreed or strongly agreed that the Data Physicalization Map helped them understand the relationship between climate change and crop yield, including 36 (58.1%) who strongly agreed. Only 2 respondents were neutral and 1 disagreed.
blocks.text: 59 of 62 participants (95.2%) agreed or strongly agreed that the Data Physicalization Map helped them understand the relationship between climate change and crop yield, including 36 (58.1%) who strongly agreed. Only 2 respondents were neutral and 1 disagreed.
blocks.zh: 62 位參與者中有 59 位（95.2%）同意或非常同意，數據實體化地圖幫助他們理解氣候變遷與作物產量之間的關係，其中 36 位（58.1%）表示非常同意。只有 2 位持中立態度，1 位不同意。

blocks.en: The sound layer reinforced this on the qualitative side. When we asked what was most memorable, one participant wrote “知道植物缺少水分的時候居然會發出聲音” (“I was surprised to learn plants make sounds when they lack water”). For these visitors, hearing the clicks made plant stress real. Several noted their surprise that a water-stressed plant produces audible clicking sounds, or named the sound of a stressed crop as the most striking part of the visit. This suggests the sound physicalization helped convey information effectively: for some visitors, the sound was the moment the abstract idea of “plant stress” became concrete.

blocks.zh: 聲音這一層在質性回饋上也強化了同樣的結果。當我們問什麼最令人印象深刻，一位參與者寫下「知道植物缺少水分的時候居然會發出聲音」。對這些參觀者而言，聽見那些喀嚓聲讓逆境變得真實。有幾位表示很驚訝缺水的植物會發出聽得見的喀嚓聲，也有人把受逆境作物的聲音列為這趟參觀最震撼的部分。這顯示聲音實體化有效地傳達了資訊：對部分參觀者來說，聲音正是「植物逆境」這個抽象概念變得具體的那一刻。

blocks.en: Finally, we looked at whether this understanding translated into intended behavior. 60 of 62 participants (96.8%) said they were willing or very willing to share what they'd learned about crop protection and agriculture with friends or family.
blocks.text: Finally, we looked at whether this understanding translated into intended behavior. 60 of 62 participants (96.8%) said they were willing or very willing to share what they'd learned about crop protection and agriculture with friends or family.

blocks.text: 18 (29.0%): joining more science-outreach or environmental activities
blocks.zh: 18 位（29.0%）：參加更多科普或環境相關活動

blocks.en: Open-ended responses echoed this: participants wrote in their own words about supporting local farmers and coffee growers, reducing carbon footprints, conserving water and energy, cutting plastic use, and educating others about climate impacts on plants.
blocks.text: Open-ended responses echoed this: participants wrote in their own words about supporting local farmers and coffee growers, reducing carbon footprints, conserving water and energy, cutting plastic use, and educating others about climate impacts on plants.
blocks.zh: 開放式回答也呼應了這一點：參與者以自己的話寫下支持在地農友與咖啡農、減少碳足跡、節約水電、減少塑膠使用，以及向他人說明氣候對植物的影響。

blocks.en: Summary
blocks.text: Summary
blocks.zh: 小結

blocks.en: Together, the three parts of the survey show what visitors understood, how their views changed, and what actions they would take. Most said they would share what they learned and would buy local farmed food. By turning invisible environmental stress into something visitors could see and hear, the exhibit made an otherwise abstract problem tangible enough that most participants left informed, and reporting an intention to change their own behavior.

blocks.zh: 三個部分的問卷合起來，呈現了參觀者理解了什麼、他們的看法如何改變，以及他們願意採取什麼行動。多數人表示會把學到的事分享出去，也會購買在地農產。把看不見的環境逆境變成參觀者看得見、聽得到的東西，這場展示讓一個原本抽象的問題變得夠具體——多數參與者離開時都帶著新的理解，也表示願意改變自己的行為。

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.text: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 結論

blocks.en: Our data physicalization booth helped us achieve our goal of making plant stress and synthetic biology more accessible, interactive, and understandable to the public. By presenting data beyond just a graph, we transformed plant-stress data into experiences that visitors could directly see, hear, and interact with. For example, our sound physicalization allowed participants to listen to recordings of stressed tobacco and tomato plants, turning an otherwise invisible biological response into something they could experience themselves. Additionally, according to our surveys, many people became more knowledgeable and aware of the effects of plant stress, with many claiming that they would relay the dire situation to family and friends as well. The physicalizations helped us bridge the gap between complex scientific concepts and everyday experiences, supporting our broader iGEM goal of communicating science beyond the scientific community.

blocks.zh: 我們的數據實體化攤位，幫助我們達成了讓植物逆境與合成生物學對大眾更可親、更互動、更好懂的目標。我們把資料呈現得不只是一張圖表，而是把植物逆境的數據變成參觀者可以直接看見、聽見並互動的體驗。例如，聲音實體化讓參與者聆聽受逆境菸草與番茄的錄音，把原本看不見的生物反應變成他們能親身體驗的東西。此外，依我們的問卷，許多人對植物逆境的影響更有知識、也更有意識，而且不少人表示會把這個嚴峻的處境轉告家人與朋友。這些實體化作品幫助我們在複雜的科學概念與日常經驗之間搭起橋梁，支持我們在 iGEM 上更大的目標：把科學傳達到科學社群之外。

attrs.en: Data Physicalization. Team members in matching shirts explain a hand-made green and yellow relief map of Taiwan to visitors crowded around the booth table.
attrs.zh: 數據實體化。穿著同款隊服的團隊成員向擠在攤位桌前的參觀者講解一張手工製作的綠黃色臺灣立體地圖。

attrs.en: The ReLEAF booth at an outdoor market. A team member points at a blue poster headed 作物的感官警報 while visitors, two of them children in caps, look on. The bioreactor prototype sits on the table beside a pair of headphones, next to the project poster.
attrs.zh: 戶外市集中的 ReLEAF 攤位。一位團隊成員指著標題為「作物的感官警報」的藍色海報，參觀者在一旁觀看，其中兩位是戴帽子的孩子。生物反應器原型放在桌上，旁邊是一副耳機與專題海報。

attrs.en: A team member holds the styrofoam map of Taiwan up against a brick wall while visitors crowd in front of it. The island is covered in dark green, yellow-green and brown paper. In the foreground a laptop and the blue sound-exhibit board stand on the table.
attrs.zh: 一位團隊成員把保麗龍製的臺灣地圖舉在磚牆前，參觀者圍在前方。島上覆滿深綠、黃綠與褐色的紙。前景的桌上放著一台筆電與藍色的聲音展件板。

attrs.en: Screenshot of the listening site. A header reads Tobacco, Drought, with a counter showing 0 of 27 clicks played. Below it a scatter plot of pitch in kilohertz against seconds into the recording, with a shaded band marked 40 to 80 kilohertz typical range, and a note that bigger dots mean louder clicks.
attrs.zh: 聆聽網站的螢幕截圖。標頭寫著「菸草，乾旱」，計數器顯示已播放 27 個喀嚓聲中的 0 個。下方是一張音高（kHz）對錄音秒數的散佈圖，有一條標示「40 至 80 kHz 典型範圍」的陰影帶，並註明點愈大代表喀嚓聲愈響。

attrs.en: A young child at the booth, seen from behind, wearing large over-ear headphones held in place by an adult beside her. Behind them on the table stand labelled water bottles.
attrs.zh: 攤位上一位從背後拍攝的幼童，戴著大型罩耳式耳機，由身旁的大人幫忙扶著。他們身後的桌上立著貼有標籤的水瓶。

attrs.en: Bar chart titled Knowledge, which region has the highest plant stress. Yilan County, marked as the correct answer, is the tallest green bar at 51.6 percent, 32 of 62 respondents. Kaohsiung is 19.4 percent, Taichung 17.7 percent and Tainan 11.3 percent, all in grey.
attrs.zh: 標題為「知識：哪一個地區的植物逆境最高」的長條圖。標示為正確答案的宜蘭縣是最高的綠色長條，為 51.6%，即 62 位受訪者中的 32 位。高雄為 19.4%、臺中 17.7%、臺南 11.3%，皆為灰色。

attrs.en: Horizontal stacked bar chart titled Attitude. Understands climate's impact on crops: 63 percent agree, 34 percent neutral, 3 percent disagree. Map helped understand the climate to yield link: 95 percent agree. More attentive to climate's agricultural impact: 98 percent agree.
attrs.zh: 標題為「態度」的水平堆疊長條圖。理解氣候對作物的影響：63% 同意、34% 中立、3% 不同意。地圖有助於理解氣候與產量的關聯：95% 同意。更關注氣候對農業的影響：98% 同意。

attrs.en: Horizontal stacked bar chart titled Practice. Willing to share knowledge with others: 97 percent agree. Selected at least one future sustainable action: 98 percent agree.
attrs.zh: 標題為「實踐」的水平堆疊長條圖。願意把知識分享給他人：97% 同意。至少選擇一項未來的永續行動：98% 同意。
